t:
(a) 
After the date of enactment of this Act, Regular Army officers shall be promoted to and appointed in the permanent grade of major general in the Regular Army only as hereinafter in this section prescribed, except in those cases governed by the provisions of section 513 of this title and except in those cases governed by the proviso to the first sentence of subsection 507 (d) of this title.
 
    (b) Based upon the number of vacancies existing and anticipated in the grade of major general in the Regular Army and the number of officers desired in that grade, the Secretary of War shall direct a selection board to select and recommend a prescribed number of officers for promotion to that grade, and, in order to insure that the Army will have adequate numbers of officers in the grade of major general with experience qualifying them for service in or with the several branches, arms, and services, he may, in his discretion, direct that, of the number to be selected and recommended, specified numbers have experience qualifying them for service in or with certain specified branches, arms, or services. The Secretary of War shall furnish to such board a list of the names of the officers to be considered. The list of names furnished for consideration shall include the name of the senior officer in the permanent grade of brigadier general whose name is not carried on the recommended list for promotion to the grade of major general and the names of additional such officers in the order that their names appear next below his on the general officers’ seniority list, as the Secretary of War may prescribe, and, until June 30, 1948, in addition thereto may include the names of any officers in permanent grade below that of major general who served during the current war in any general officer grade under temporary appointment. From among the. officers named for consideration, the designated selection board shall select and recommend the prescribed number, including any prescribed numbers whose experience qualifies them for service in or with a designated branch, arm, or service. The officers selected and recommended shall be those who, in the opinion of the board, are the best qualified officers of those listed for consideration.
 
    (c) The names of officers who are selected and recommended for promotion to the grade of major general in the Regular Army shall be carried on a permanent recommended list of officers for promotion to that grade. Upon selection, the names of such officers shall be placed on the recommended list at the foot thereof arranged among themselves according to precedence to be determined by the Secretary of War. The number of officers to be selected and recommended by designated selection boards for promotion to the grade of major general in the Regular Army shall be determined by the Secretary of War. It is not mandatory that the Secretary of War direct the selection and recommendation of numbers sufficient to produce the number authorized for that grade; but officers who are selected and recommended for promotion to that grade by any such selection board, and whose names are not removed from the recommended list by the President, shall be nominated, and by and with the advice and consent of the Senate appointed, in that grade as soon as there is a vacancy in the number authorized for that grade.
 
    (d) The ratio of the. number of officers which the Secretary of War names for consideration by any selection board for promotion to the grade of major general in the Regular Army, to the number of officers which he directs such selection board to select from among those so named, may be as desired by the Secretary of War, but no officer shall be considered or selected by any selection board more than one year prior to the date on which it is anticipated he will, if selected, be appointed in that grade. After June 30, 1949, officers must have completed at least one year’s service under permanent appointment in the grade of brigadier general in the Regular Army, before being nominated or appointed in the grade of major general in the Regular Army.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "selection board" making recommendations resembles an advisory board, but this is an internal Army promotion board that recommends officers for major general, and nothing in the text suggests it includes non-federal members. Every actor involved (the Secretary of War, the selection board, the President, the Senate) is inside the federal government. No public comment, hearing, rulemaking, outside consultation, or right to sue is provided.
fable.s: the Secretary of War shall direct a selection board to select and recommend a prescribed number of officers for promotion to that grade

qwen_block.w: This section describes an internal military promotion process where a selection board chooses from among Regular Army officers. All parties involved (the Secretary of War, the selection board, and the officers being considered) are part of the federal government. There is no consultation or coordination with entities outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, or the general public.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of War shall direct a selection board to select and recommend a prescribed number of officers for promotion to that grade... The Secretary of War shall furnish to such board a list of the names of the officers to be considered.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "selection board" constitutes an advisory body involving outside experts or public participation. However, the text specifies that the board selects from a list of "Regular Army officers" provided by the Secretary of War. These are federal employees/officers. The process is an internal military personnel management procedure (promotion selection), not a consultation with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private companies). Therefore, it falls under the "No" category for intra-government coordination/decision-making.

opus.w: Every actor in this promotion process is inside the federal government. The Secretary of War, the Army selection board, the President and the Senate (through advice and consent) are all federal. The selection board may look like an advisory panel, but it is an internal military body with no non-federal members. Since no one outside the government takes part in the promotion decision, this is not participation.
opus.s: the Secretary of War shall direct a selection board to select and recommend a prescribed number of officers for promotion to that grade
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The section sets up a "selection board" that recommends officers for promotion, and the Senate gives "advice and consent." Both look like outside input into a federal decision.

**Why it fails:** Everyone involved is inside the federal government. The selection board is an internal Army body directed by the Secretary of War, made up of military officers who are federal personnel doing their jobs. The Senate is part of Congress, which also counts as inside the government. No state, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, so no outside party takes part in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes an internal military promotion process where a selection board, directed by the Secretary of War, recommends officers for promotion. All actors involved (Secretary of War, selection board members, officers) are part of the federal government (specifically the military). There is no consultation or coordination with entities outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of War shall direct a selection board to select and recommend a prescribed number of officers for promotion to that grade... The Secretary of War shall furnish to such board a list of the names of the officers to be considered.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "selection board" constitutes an advisory body involving outside experts or stakeholders participating in the promotion decision. However, the text specifies that the board is directed by the Secretary of War and selects from a list of officers provided by the Secretary. These are internal military personnel and federal officials. There is no mention of state governments, the general public, private companies, or independent experts outside the federal government being involved in the selection process. The process is entirely intra-governmental (military hierarchy).
